title: fix(training)!: treat max_steps as the global step target
bug_description:
## Summary

`Trainer(max_steps=...)` counted updates per fit call, so a resumed fit trained `max_steps` more steps. That went past
the configured total and past learning-rate schedules sized with `max_steps`. Following Lightning, `max_steps` is now
the global optimizer step at which training stops.

## Changes

- A fit resumed from step `N` runs `max_steps - N` updates. When the restored step already reaches `max_steps`, the
  fit runs its start and end hooks without training, logs "`Trainer.fit` stopped: `max_steps=...` reached", and
  returns `iterations=0`.
- Metrics log at global steps divisible by `log_every_n_steps`, plus the first step of each fit. Fresh runs log exactly

- `TQDMProgressBar` and `RichProgressBar` start at the restored step instead of `0`.
- `weights_only=True` fits start at step `0`, so transfer learning is unchanged.

title: Bugfix: a long loop of engines ran out of file descriptors
bug_description:
* Every engine start left two sockets open: the listener that MDI_Init opens and
  the connection to the engine, which pymdi has no call to close. A job that
  started many engines -- one per species in a Thermochemistry CBH ladder, about
  100 in 13 iterations -- then ran out of file descriptors (256 for a macOS
  JobServer) and could start no more engines, failing with "nodename nor
  servname provided, or not known". The engine's sockets are now closed when it
  is closed, and after a failed start.
* A local engine now dials back to the loopback address 127.0.0.1 rather than
  "localhost", so that no name lookup is needed.
* Starting is tried four times, waiting 2, 10 and 30 seconds between attempts
  (before, three times within three seconds), to ride out a short outage.

title: Read a ledger with no schema yet as empty under missing_ok
bug_description:
On a fresh workspace, `ginkgo run --detach` can fail with `.ginkgo/ginkgo.db has not been initialized yet`.

## Cause

The detached child's first run creates `.ginkgo/ginkgo.db` before it writes the schema. Meanwhile the parent polls for the run row with `query.open(missing_ok=True)`. If the parent reads inside that window, it gets `UninitializedStoreError`, not an empty ledger, and `run --detach` exits 1. That's what failed `test_a_detached_run_can_be_waited_for` on #415's CI ([run](https://github.com/sanjaynagi/ginkgo/actions/runs/40729717468/job/122962425424)). `runs status`, `history` and `why` hit the same window if they read during a first run.

## Fix

`query.open(missing_ok=True)` now treats a ledger with no schema yet the same as a missing one, and returns an empty ledger. Without `missing_ok`, it still raises.

bug_description:
<!-- Read docs/contributing.md before opening your PR. -->

## Issue

A tester's phone could no longer connect to the BLE setup service. It held a stale bond with the robot, Android's automatic re-pairing was refused with SMP "Numeric comparison failed (0x0c)", and every connect failed until the user forgot the robot in the phone's settings.

## Description

常駐数の上限（resident cap）の2つの穴を、おぷー決定（2026-10-29）の方針で塞ぐ。

## Summary

`to_datatree()` passed `num_chains` straight to `_reshape_chains()`, so `num_chains=0` failed with a bare `ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero`, and a negative value that divides the sample count failed in `reshape` with `ValueError: can only specify one unknown dimension`. title: fix(nsoc): keep progress totals current across overlapping completion batches
bug_description:
Fixes #3182

The progress summary (`useUserProgress`) batches completions with a 3s debounce and sends them to `/progress/bulk-update/`. When a second completion was queued while an earlier batch request was still in flight, the earlier request's `onSettled` invalidated `["userProgress"]` and cleared the rollback snapshot. The refetch returned server totals that did not include the newer, not-yet-sent completion, so the optimistic cache was overwritten and the summary showed the previous total until a manual refresh. The cause is client-side cache invalidation, not the API aggregation.

Fix: track in-flight bulk requests and skip the invalidate/snapshot-clear in `onSettled` while another batch is in flight or queued. The last batch to settle does the refetch.

title: fix(pipeline): drop page backend references on unload

Shared diagnostics show it 7 times on 25-28 Oct, each time right after a USB base update and each time on a sync that carried a planned active digest. bug_description:
Closes #757

## 이번에 한 일

배포로 BE 가 내려갈 때 메모리에 남은 전사·측정 기록을 저장하기 전에 컨테이너가 강제로 끝내지 않도록 종료 시간을 맞췄습니다.

- 연습 연결(스트림)을 하나씩 기다리지 않고 같이 닫습니다. 연결 수와 관계없이 최대 5초입니다(기존은 연결마다 5초).
- 1초 원자료·확정 전사·문장 끝 신호·코치 이벤트를 한 단계에서 같이 저장합니다. `flush_metrics` 도 확정 전사를 원자료와 같이 저장해 DB 가 느릴 때 상한이 5초+5초가 아니라 5초입니다.
- 끝내기 정리(자동 종료·떠난 Take)를 기다리는 상한은 `stop_all` 을 시작한 때부터 잽니다. 연결 정리·기록 저장과 같이 돌고 있었기 때문입니다.
- uvicorn 이 열린 요청을 기다리는 시간을 5초로 정했습니다(`--timeout-graceful-shutdown 5`). 기본값은 끝없이 기다려 기록 저장이 그만큼 밀립니다.
- 앱 종료 상한을 `main.shutdown_max_sec()` 으로 계산하고 compose 의 `stop_grace_period` 를 45초로 정했습니다. 요청 대기 5초 + 앱 종료 최대 33초(연결·기록·끝내기 정리 18초, 코치 10초, 분석 5초)입니다. 셋이 어긋나면 `tests/test_shutdown_budget.py` 가 실패합니다.

## 리뷰에서 봐주셨으면 하는 곳

- `registry.stop_all` 에서 기록 저장과 `coach.shutdown` 을 한 번에 돌립니다. 둘은 다른 테이블에 쓰고 `shutdown` 은 문장 끝 목록을 건드리지 않아 순서가 필요 없다고 봤습니다.
- `flush_metrics` 는 Take 를 끝낼 때도 부릅니다. 확정 전사 저장이 원자료 저장과 같이 돌게 되는데 이 순서에 기대는 곳이 있는지 봐주세요.

## 고민했던 점 · 다른 선택지

- 대기 시간만 늘리면 연결 수가 늘 때 다시 모자랍니다. 그래서 먼저 연결을 같이 닫고 저장을 묶어 상한을 연결 수와 무관하

title: 🐛 fix(reinstall): give back links after a failure
bug_description:
A failed rebuild during a parallel `pipx reinstall-all` no longer leaves the restored environment without a shared app, man page or completion link. This closes the gap #2321 left open for #2312.

While `reinstall-all` rebuilds an environment, the old one sits in the trash and its exposed links dangle until the new environment directory exists, for example while shared libraries are upgraded.
```python
FORGET_ACTIONS = ("silent", "archive", "unlink")        # forget 实际写这个
JOURNAL_ACTIONS = (..., "silence", "archive", ...)       # 声明的是 silence
```

`forget.apply` 写的是 `db._journal(conn, d.action, ...)`，`d.action` 来自 `FORGET_ACTIONS` —— 所以库里真实出现的是 `silent`，而白名单声明的是 `silence`。**两者永远对不上，谁也没报错。**

`conflict` 在 `JOURNAL_ACTIONS` 里声明了，代码里从未产生。L4 自述「记录所有状态变更」，实际漏了最该留痕的一类 —— 用户的事实被判定冲突、旧的被下线，库里一个字都没记。

```text
### Why

`main` CI, and every merge-queue run since, fails `tests/harness/test_skill_examples.py` on a `lowest-versions` shard:

```
UserWarning: Framing tag 'plan_reminder' was registered after framing tags were first escaped, ...
```

`pydantic_ai_harness.planning._toolset` registers `plan_reminder` at import time, but the harness imports `Planning` lazily, through the package `__getattr__`. In a test process, the first import of `Planning` can come after another test has already escaped framing text, and `register_tag` then warns, which `filterwarnings = error` turns into a failure. Whether that happens depends only on which modules share a shard. The shard split is based on module durations, and the most recent merge changed them, so this ordering now occurs.
```

title: 🐛 fix(expose): replace links to dropped apps
bug_description:
Before 1.18.0 (#2097), upgrading a package whose new release dropped an app left that app's link in `PIPX_BIN_DIR`, pointing at a file that no longer exists. #2315 moved the read to [run on every call](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/41a92f1390b7310b6241659002ac2f3345f9af93/src/pipx/commands/ensure_path.py#L135), `--force` included, and decoded it as UTF-8. 1.18.7 [read the file only without `--force`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/commands/ensure_path.py#L134), so `--force` never decoded it. title: 🐛 fix(run): free the cache lock before uv run
bug_description:
On Windows under the uv backend, a second `pipx run script.py` of the same PEP 723 script waited, with no message, until the first one exited, and a script that ran itself through pipx never finished. Now pipx releases its run-cache lock before handing the script to `uv run`, so concurrent runs start right away, as they do on POSIX and did in 1.18.7.

#2274 moved uv script environments into pipx's run cache and [called `run_script_via_uv_run` inside `_locked_venv_cache`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1741e6aaca3317ce3bc13c93f48c9278bc7f4241/src/pipx/commands/run.py#L165-L181). bug_description:
## Summary
Follow-up to merged PR #287 for the queued plan-acceptance identity regression. This does not close #245, which is already closed.

## Root cause and approach
Acceptance boundaries carried plan ID and version but dropped the proposal fingerprint; Web/TUI text acceptance could also read a proposal only after its worker was queued. This change snapshots ID/version/fingerprint at CLI, Web, and TUI ingress, carries it through queued execution, and rechecks all three fields before acceptance. The persistence transaction compares the expected proposal identity while atomically committing the Working Plan and acceptance event. Web structured actions and the Go TUI send the fingerprint. A request is primed when an `on_model_request_error` hook exists, for example with `ModelFallback`: the agent opens the stream and reads its first event before handing it to the consumer. If the consumer then leaves the stream without iterating it, for example by exiting `node.stream()` straight away, `release_primed_segment()` closed the primed segment and dropped it.

title: 🐛 fix(inspect): skip looping editable man pages
bug_description:

title: 🐛 fix(transaction): hold signals during a restore
bug_description:
Pressing Ctrl-C a second time while pipx rolled back a failed `reinstall`, `install --force`, `inject`, `upgrade` or `manifest sync`, or getting `SIGTERM`/`SIGHUP` during a rollback, could lose the environment. The rollback deleted the half-built environment and then renamed the backup into place ([old restore](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/51cd6c71b1375ed00e5834874f2e9f49c9b2a330/src/pipx/commands/transaction.py#L69-L72)), and a signal between the two steps left `venvs/<name>` gone with its only copy in the trash, which the next pipx command emptied. Now the restore always completes, and pipx acts on the signal right after. Fixes #2328.

### Why it happened

pipx turns SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP into `KeyboardInterrupt` for the whole command, so one could raise out of the `rmtree` or between it and the `rename`. The new `uninterrupted()` context manager ([source](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/2ac1394524b54ea1545f29a3920bc574317b9713/src/pipx/fanout.py#L73-L94)) swaps in a hand

title: 🐛 fix(venv): refuse installers without pyvenv.cfg
bug_description:
When an environment lost its `pyvenv.cfg`, pipx kept [pointing pip or uv at `<venv>/bin/python`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/backends/uv.py#L217-L226), which without that file is the interpreter the venv was created from. `pipx upgrade` then installed the package into that interpreter's prefix, such as `/usr/local` for root, reported success, and `pipx uninstall` left the files behind. Every backend operation receives the venv's interpreter path from `Venv`, and nothing checked that the directory was still a virtual environment; uv's own guard against system interpreters is off when `--python` is explicit. [`Venv._installer_python`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/c6a8452a7

bug_description:
When a package declared a command, man page or completion name that something else already held, `pipx install` kept the existing file and warned "File exists … Not modifying". The next `pipx reinstall`, `reinstall-all`, `interpreter upgrade`, repair step of `pipx upgrade`, or repeated `pipx manifest sync` then deleted that file and linked the package's script in its place, with no warning and no `--force` from the user ([old line](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/commands/common.py#L272)). Now a rebuild replaces only what the environment exposed before, and everything else keeps its owner, as `pipx uninstall` followed by `pipx install` does. Fixes #2312.

title: 🐛 fix(cli): reject shared flags before nested cmd
bug_description:
`pipx manifest --global sync --prune`, `pipx cache --global purge` and `pipx interpreter --global prune` [accepted `--global` and then dropped it](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/main.py#L772-L776), so the command changed the caller's per-user store with exit 0 and left the global one alone. Now that position fails with `unrecognized arguments: --global`, exactly as `pipx --global install` already does, and the documented position after the subcommand works as before. `--skip-maintenance`, `-v` and `-q` get the same treatment. Fixes #2319.

### Cause

The group parsers and their subcommand parsers both inherited `shared_parser`, and argparse copies the subcommand's namespace, defaults included, over the group's, so `is_global=False` from `sync` overwrote the `True` parsed by `manifest`. The fix drops `parents=[shared_parser]` from the [`manifest`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/a629d05dc0d7f59c14a177e155c316b8098de5ba/src/pipx/main

title: 🐛 fix(runpip): run the installer in the working dir
bug_description:
Since 1.12.0, `pipx runpip ENV install -r requirements.txt` looked for `requirements.txt` in `$PIPX_HOME/venvs/ENV` instead of the directory the user ran it from, because [`run_raw_pip` always started the installer in the venv root](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/backends/pip.py#L183-L206). Relative paths usually failed with file-not-found, and when an installed wheel had shipped a data file under the same name, pip or uv read that file and ignored the user's. `pipx runpip` now runs the installer in the caller's working directory on both backends, as it did before 1.12.0. Fixes #2317.

### Cause

The backend split (#1806) routed both pipx's own pip calls and `pipx runpip` through `run_raw_pip`, and gave all of them the venv root as working directory. That is right for the calls whose arguments pipx builds, and wrong for `runpip`, whose arguments the user wrote for their own directory. `run_raw_pip` now takes `in_working_dir` ([pip](h

title: 🐛 fix(main): drop launcher dir from sys.path
bug_description:
With pipx installed by `pip install --user pipx`, an installed app whose script was named like a module pipx imports, such as `json.py` or `shlex.py`, [was imported by pipx itself](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/__main__.py#L7-L37), because the launcher's directory `~/.local/bin` comes first on `sys.path`. An exposed `json.py` broke every later pipx command, `uninstall` included. Now pipx drops that entry at start-up, so files next to its launcher, or in the working directory under `python -m pipx`, cannot shadow its imports. Fixes #2314.

### Cause

Python adds the started script's directory (the working directory under `-m`) to the front of `sys.path`, and pip's launcher is a plain script in the directory pipx links apps into. [`pipx/__main__.py` now removes that entry](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/7172431802b9ec675ad9322a824ac0ab8a107e1c/src/pipx/__main__.py#L10-L26) before `import pathlib`, the first import the interpreter h
author: gaborbernat

title: 🐛 fix(ensurepath): keep foreign global PATH file
bug_description:
`pipx ensurepath --global` used to [overwrite](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/commands/ensure_path.py#L134-L150) `/etc/profile.d/pipx.sh` (or `/etc/paths.d/pipx` on macOS) with its single `PATH` entry whenever the file differed from it, so an administrator's `PIPX_GLOBAL_*` or `PIP_INDEX_URL` exports kept there disappeared while pipx printed `Success!`. Now pipx leaves such a file and its mode untouched and exits 1 with an error that names the file and `--force`. A file that holds only an earlier pipx entry is still replaced, including when the bin directory or append/prepend changes. Fixes #2313.

### Cause

The only thing that marked the file as pipx's was its name. `_ensure_global_path()` now [reads the existing file and refuses](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/9a8ff786d50d20e8cd76ea2d6f0e2f52561b1d56/src/pipx/commands/ensure_path.py#L135-L147) unless it is empty or [matches an entry pipx writes](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blo
author: gaborbernat

title: 🐛 fix(shared): apply --cooldown to the shared pip
bug_description:
With `--cooldown` or `PIPX_COOLDOWN` under the pip backend, pipx held back the package being installed but [installed or refreshed the shared pip](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/shared_libs.py#L295-L317) with no age limit, so a pip uploaded minutes earlier could land in the environment every pip-backed venv runs. That happened on the first pip-backed command in a new pipx home and after each 30-day refresh. The shared pip now honors the same cooldown as the rest of the command. Fixes #2310.

### Cause

The cooldown reached installer arguments only through `Venv._with_cooldown`, which package installs call; the shared-libs code saw `pip_args` and nothing else. The command's resolved cooldown now [reaches the shared libraries](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/c88e17df599eea9d4e1b9eea9318c33a1f4574cb/src/pipx/main.py#L436) the way `--skip-maintenance` already does, and [`_install_pip`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/c88e17df599eea9d
author: gaborbernat

title: 🐛 fix(self-install): resolve both sides for bin dir
bug_description:
A self-managed pipx started through its environment's own script with a `..` or symlinked path, such as `../share/pipx/venvs/pipx/bin/pipx` from `~/.local/bin`, [took `venvs/pipx/bin` as its bin directory](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/self_install.py#L46-L52). Apps it installed were linked there, off `PATH`, and a script named like a stdlib module could shadow that module inside pipx. Now every spelling of the venv's script falls back to `~/.local/bin`, while the exposed `pipx` link keeps recovering its own directory. Fixes #2308.

### Cause

The check meant "a file outside the venv that resolves into it", but tested the outside half lexically on an unnormalized `argv[0]`, so `bin/../venvs/pipx/bin/pipx` looked outside. [It now compares real locations on both sides](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/d597fd846e489e84316f7112135e13900a30ec57/src/pipx/self_install.py#L47-L55): the resolved directory of the invoked file must lie outsid
author: gaborbernat

title: 🐛 fix(cli): refuse option-shaped package values
bug_description:
`pipx install --preinstall=-rFILE` and `pipx run --with=--find-links=DIR script.py` passed the value to pip or `uv pip install` as an installer option, because [`--preinstall`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/commands/install.py#L1064-L1065) and [script `--with`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/commands/run.py#L143) skip spec parsing. Such a value changed the index, the links source or the target directory with no error. Now pipx refuses it before any installer runs and points to `--pip-args`. Fixes #2305.

### Cause

The backends build `[*pip_args, *requirements]`, which is safe only when every requirement went through `_parse_specifier`. These two options keep the string as typed: `--preinstall` so its version specifier survives, script `--with` so its markers do. Rather than parse them (which would strip those), [`_package_spec`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/221eb008cbccf4ca0
author: gaborbernat

title: 🐛 fix(uninject): skip invalid distribution names
bug_description:
`pipx uninject` takes the orphaned dependencies it removes from installed metadata and [passed their names to the installer unchecked](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/venv_inspect.py#L75-L79). A `Name` such as `-t/some/dir` reached `uv pip uninstall` as an option, and uv then uninstalled packages from that directory while pipx reported success. Now pipx ignores any distribution whose `Name` is not a valid project name, so only real package names reach the uninstall command. Fixes #2304.

### Cause

[`_distribution_name()`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/a6b8072192cd1ded22ba5fadd0658ddea46175f7/src/pipx/venv_inspect.py#L75-L80) returned `dist.name` as written, and the callers canonicalized it without validation, which keeps a leading `-` and `/`. It now returns `canonicalize_name(name, validate=True)` and treats an invalid name like a missing one, as `venv.py`'s helper of the same name already does for `.dist-info` directory names.

title: 🐛 fix(expose): keep dangling links of live venvs
bug_description:
When two environments exposed the same command, man page, or completion name, a plain `pipx upgrade-all` could move it to the other environment without `--force`: pipx [replaced any link whose target was missing](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/commands/common.py#L294-L296), and the owner's link dangles for a moment while its installer rewrites the file. `_symlink_package_resource()` read "target missing" as "left over, nobody's". The [new check](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/c3aab53b7094f026dea7abb43c2f9e3cf8750de0/src/pipx/commands/common.py#L314-L323) treats a dangling link as a [collision](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/c3aab53b7094f026dea7abb43c2f9e3cf8750de0/src/pipx/commands/common.py#L279-L280) when it points into a directory under `P

title: 🐛 fix(interpreter): keep upgrade on standalone
bug_description:
`pipx interpreter upgrade` could [rebuild an environment on another Python from `PATH`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/commands/interpreter.py#L173-L181) when the package's newest release had a `Requires-Python` that ruled out the new standalone build, and still print `app: 3.14.9 -> 3.14.10` with exit 0. The call [now passes `python_flag_passed=True`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/b07c55df8d5bda6e115a75e3777504e20047e15e/src/pipx/commands/interpreter.py#L173-L183), so the rebuild raises, `reinstall()` restores the environment from its backup, and the

title: 🐛 fix(run): end uv options before the app name
bug_description:
Under the uv backend, `pipx run -- -n pycowsay hi` or `pipx run -- -ihttp://host/simple demodep` let uv read the dash-leading app word as one of its own options and then install and run the next word as the package, because the app was [appended right after uv's options](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/commands/run_uv.py#L81-L85). `run_via_uv_tool_run` built `uv tool run [options] APP ARGS…` without ending option parsing. It [now inserts `--`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/2fcfbb878b5403340c87532b322ed69f400f46d6/src/pipx/commands/run_uv.py#L83-L84) before the app, so every word from the app on is passed through verbatim.

title: 🐛 fix(transaction): spare backups still in use
bug_description:
Running any pipx command, even `pipx list`, while a `reinstall`, `reinstall-all`, `install --force`, `upgrade` or `inject` was still running deleted that command's rollback backup, because every command emptied the trash at startup ([old line](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/main.py#L2191)). title: 🐛 fix(uninject): keep links other packages expose

title: 🐛 fix(run): expire script cache on venv failure
bug_description:
If `python -m venv` failed or was interrupted during the first `pipx run script.py`, [`run_script`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/commands/run.py#L201-L214) kept the half-built cache directory, and every later run of that script failed with `FileNotFoundError` for `bin/python` until the entry expired. The `try` that writes `pipx_expired_venv` covered only `install_unmanaged_packages`, while the reuse check is whether the directory exists, and the directory exists before `python -m venv` starts. `create_venv` [now runs inside that `try`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/4aa390c2ef640405641c6e41b3e0e53dd8ae5f00/src/pipx/commands/run.py#L206-L214), matching what `run_package` does since #2235.

title: 🐛 fix(standalone): lock per-version python fetch
bug_description:
Two pipx commands fetching the same standalone Python at once, such as parallel CI steps with `--fetch-python`, could leave `PIPX_HOME/py/X.Y` with part of its standard library missing, because both [staged the build in one fixed directory and cleared it as a leftover](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/standalone_python.py#L134-L148). pipx kept using that broken interpreter for every later install. Now the second command waits for the first and reuses its build, and `pipx interpreter prune` no longer deletes a fetch that is still running. Fixes #2291.

With the temporary directory on another filesystem, moving the unpacked build into `py/.X.Y.incoming` is a file-by-file copy, and a second fetch deleted that directory while the first was still filling it. [`download_python_build_standalone()`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/189626fb9c37bc7a962f1659c1f67baf49edd3ac/src/pipx/standalone_python.py#L110-L142) now holds [a per-ve

title: 🐛 fix(fanout): wait for tasks when output breaks
bug_description:
When the output of `pipx reinstall-all`, `upgrade-all`, or `install-all` went to a reader that quit early (`| head`, a closed pager) or to a stderr closed at startup, pipx logged a traceback and returned while worker threads were still rebuilding environments, because [replaying a held task's output](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/fanout.py#L340-L347) raised. An interrupt in that window skipped the rollback and lost the environment's metadata, and a task waiting for its turn hung pipx. Now pipx waits for every task, each held task gets its turn, and a broken stream is reported by the task that writes to it next. Fixes #2288.

### Cause

[`go_live()`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/93ecb22a179834824354299bdc998a440d1741be/src/pipx/fanout.py#L340-L350) marked the slot live only after every buffered write succeeded. The write error escaped from `_wait_in_order()`, then again from `_settle()` in `fan_out()`'s `finally`, before it wait
author: gaborbernat

title: 🐛 fix(pip): refuse lock installs on pip below 26.1

title: 🐛 fix(standalone): follow links in tar fallback
bug_description:
When pipx itself runs on CPython 3.11.0 to 3.11.3, it unpacks fetched standalone Python builds with [its own validator](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/standalone_python.py#L235-L249) because `tarfile.data_filter` is missing there. ### Cause

The check compared paths as text with `os.path.normpath()`, while extraction goes through the filesystem and follows links unpacked a moment earlier. [`_escapes()`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/ad5296ff73b37a7fcd0da1b0f82bc96331af159a/src/pipx/standalone_python.py#L252-L264) now resolves the longest existing prefix of the path with a strict `realpath`, so a loop or an overlong chain co

title: 🐛 fix(inspect): skip installed-files.txt by RECORD
bug_description:
A dependency, or a package injected without `--include-apps`, could ship an `installed-files.txt` into the main package's `.dist-info` and have its own commands, man pages and completions linked as the main package's, with no `--include-deps`. pipx [read that file for every distribution](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/aed1d303cda2652d603f6ef122cb8195d34172e6/src/pipx/venv_inspect.py#L190). Now it reads it only for a distribution without a `RECORD`, and the main package exposes only what it installed. Fixes #2276.

### Cause

`installed-files.txt` is the file list of a legacy `setup.py install` egg-info, and wheel installers never write it. [`get_resources_from_inst_files()`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/13526e5ad47aed3e1d2854665fba0b41d62d926c/src/pipx/venv_inspect.py#L183-L203) now skips it when the distribution has a `RECORD`. `importlib.metadata.Distribution.files` uses the same rule, except that pipx also treats an empty `RECORD` as present, the stricter of the two readings

title: 🐛 fix(venv): keep pipx's record across installer runs
bug_description:

bug_description:

title: Keep re-auth cookies from being overwritten by the old session
bug_description:
A re-auth or reconfigure could be undone by the session it replaces.

`NestSessionManager` reports `client.refreshed_cookies` after every Google token exchange, including failed or cancelled ones (#641). `refreshed_cookies` keeps the last rotated value, and `_persist_refreshed_cookies` wrote it whenever it differed from the entry. After a re-auth stores new cookies, any later exchange by the old manager therefore wrote its old cookies back over them. That includes an exchange that's still running when the reload cancels it, which is likely while a failing session is retrying Google. The callback is now created per session manager (`_cookie_persister`) and only writes while the entry still holds the cookies that manager loaded or last wrote. Anything else came from a re-auth or reconfigure and is left alone.

title: Answer refused interface requests before closing the connection
bug_description:
﻿## What changes and why

When the local interface's server refused a request (another origin, a missing or wrong
session key, or a body that is not JSON), it answered and closed the connection **without
reading the request body**. Closing a socket that still holds unread data makes the operating
system reset the connection. On Windows the reset could reach the client before the answer,
so the client saw "connection aborted" instead of the refusal.

`test_requests_without_the_key_or_from_other_origins_are_refused` failed about once in twenty
runs on Windows because of this, and it already failed once in a local `/push` verification
during this milestone.

The server now reads and drops the rest of a refused request's body, up to 1 MiB
(`DISCARD_BYTES`), before it closes the connection. Requests that were already read are not
read twice, and larger bodies are not read at all.

Closes #23

`write_required()` reported a write on unchanged entities that hold dates with a month or year precision. ## Description

When a conversation holding offloaded previews lands on a stash that doesn't have the originals, the stash write path files each preview under its original's key, because a truncated tool result keeps its `toolUseId`. `retrieve_context` then serves the preview as the original, and the model reports "No matches found" for content that exists. title: Make the device sensor's available attribute show whether the device answers successfully
bug_description:
A device without alarms and timers, such as a Chromecast Audio, showed `available: false` on its device sensor for as long as the integration ran, even while it answered every update. The attribute was `true` only when the last request for alarms, settings or a reboot got a successful answer. A device without alarms answers "not found" when asked for alarms. title: fix: keep the PICS lead in its credible set and clamp r2 drifting above 1
bug_description:
## ✨ Context

Fixes the two PICS problems in opentargets/issues#4607. Both come from the lead not being treated as the anchor of its own credible set:

1. A panel `r` a few ulps past ±1 gives `r2Overall` above 1. The float32 cast in `annotate_ld` hides drift below ~6e-8, but an `r` of 1.0000001 still squares to `1.0000002` in float32. PICS then computes `sd = sqrt(negative) = NaN` for that tag.
2. PICS sorted members by `(posterior DESC, variantId)`. Perfect proxies tie with the lead, so when enough of them sort before it by `variantId`, the coverage cut drops the lead from its own credible set.

title: Fix Linux x86-64 startup on older kernels
bug_description:
## Summary

On older x86-64 Linux kernels, ty 0.0.93 aborts in `ld.so` before it reaches `main`. Preserving the ELF layout that those kernels expect adds 2.06 MiB to the installed executable, but only 4.33 KiB to the wheel.

BOLT moves the ELF program header table after `.bss`. The loader reserves memory for `.bss` and fills it with zeros, so those bytes take up no space in the file. title: Fix watchdog shutdown timing, add unreachable shutdown
bug_description:
В логике watchdog обнаружено несоответствие между временем, которое показывается в уведомлениях, и фактическим моментом, когда выполняется shutdown.

## Проблема:
- отображение оставшегося времени считалось отдельно от проверки истечения cooldown
- shutdown проверялся по одному выражению, а оставшееся время — по другому
- из-за усечения int(...) и шагов таймера получалось, что в логах появляется 0 seconds left, но выключение происходит на следующем тике

- введён единый deadline для таймера: deadline = empty_since + wd_poweroff_cooldown
- оставшееся время вычисляется по формуле remaining = max(0, ceil(deadline - now))
- shutdown выполняется только при now >= deadline
- предупреждение о скором выключении теперь использует тот же самый расчёт времени, что и фактическое выключение
- исправлены формулировки в логах и UX на более соответствующие реально происходящим процессам
- добавлено выключение VPS, если Minecraft сервер недоступен дольше WATCHDOG_UNREACHABLE_SECONDS

## Description

### Bug & Root Cause
In `tensormap-backend/app/routers/health.py`, the `/ready` readiness probe endpoint caught database connection errors and returned `{"status": "not ready", "database": "disconnected"}`. However, because no HTTP status code was set, FastAPI defaulted to returning HTTP 200 OK.
Kubernetes readiness probes, Docker healthchecks, and reverse proxy load balancers rely on non-2xx HTTP status codes to detect failure. Returning HTTP 200 deceived ingress controllers and orchestration systems into routing traffic to instances with broken or disconnected database connections.

- Injected FastAPI's `Response` dependency into `readiness_check()`.

title: 🔒 fix(run): keep the backend after a failed install
bug_description: When a `pipx run` on the uv backend failed inside `uv pip install`, the half-built venv stayed in the run cache without `pipx_metadata.json`. On the next identical command, [`Venv.__init__`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/venv.py#L200-L211) saw a non-empty directory and passed the unread `PipxMetadata` default, `"pip"`, as the recorded backend. pipx then installed with pip, which ignores `UV_INDEX_URL`, the setting [our docs](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/docs/how-to/use-private-index.rst#L38-L40) tell uv users to use for a private index. A user who named their private index that way got the package from pip's default index (PyPI), so anyone who registered the internal name there had their code run as that user. After this PR a directory without a readable record resolves its backend like a new venv, and a failed `pipx run` install expires its cache entry so the retry starts from scratch.

title: 🐛 fix(reinstall): refuse to guess an unrecorded source
bug_description:
When an environment had no readable `pipx_metadata.json`, `reinstall` fell back to the directory name ([`reinstall.py#L217-L220`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/commands/reinstall.py#L217-L220), [`venv.py#L295-L300`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/venv.py#L295-L300)) and installed it with no pip arguments. `reinstall-all` and `repair` go through the same function. A user whose tool came from `--index-url`, a URL, a local path or a suffixed install got the default index's release under the directory name instead; pipx exited 0 and recorded the bare name, so later upgrades kept using the default index. After this PR those commands refuse such an environment with the "missing internal pipx metadata" advice `upgrade` gives, and only pre-0.15 environments keep the old fallback. Fixes #2204.

title: 🔒 fix(upgrade): record --find-links as absolute
bug_description: `pipx upgrade --pip-args` passed a relative `--find-links` or `--constraint` to the installer and [stored it as typed](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/venv.py#L818-L828). Another local account that could write a `wheels/` subdirectory there, for example in `/tmp`, got its wheel installed as pipx's shared pip or as the environment's command, and run as the invoking user (root for `--global`). With this PR, pipx stores the absolute path at upgrade time, resolves relative values already on record against the environment's own directory, and runs the shared pip refresh inside the shared libraries directory. This addresses [draft advisory ANT-2026-GPDEK73X](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/security/advisories/GHSA-79wq

title: 🐛 fix(install-all): translate abbreviated pip args
bug_description:

A user who installed from a private index with `--pip-args "--index-u URL"` got the index dropped on replay, and uv installed the same name and version from its default index, exiting 0. After this PR, abbreviations pip accepts translate the same as the full spelling. Fixes #2207.

title: 🔒 fix(runpip): record the index runpip installed from
bug_description: After a successful `pipx runpip ENV install` that replaces the main package, pipx rewrites the recorded `package_or_url` from the runpip command line, but [builds the new `pip_args` from the old record alone](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/commands/run_pip.py#L145-L149). Take a tool installed from a local wheel and later moved with `pipx runpip corp-tool install --upgrade --index-url COMPANY corp-tool`: pipx records the bare name `corp-tool` with no index. The next `pipx upgrade`, `upgrade-all` or `reinstall` resolves that name on the installer's default index, PyPI unless configured otherwise. Whoever publishes `corp-tool` there gets their code installed behind the tool's command, and it runs as the user. With this PR the index options from the runpip command go into the record, so later commands ask the same index. This addresses [draft advisory ANT-2026-QKQWS7KD](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/security/advisories/GHSA-rp6q-c7v8-fr6q

title: 🔒 fix(log): create log files owner-only
bug_description:

After this PR the log directory is 0700 and every log file is 0600, so only the owner reads them. This addresses [draft advisory ANT-2026-FAYJOIBW](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/security/advisories/GHSA-grq3-49f2-55w5).

title: 🐛 fix(install): restore venv after a failed --force
bug_description:
`pipx install --force` backed up the existing environment only for `--app`, `--include-resources-from`, a lock file or `manifest sync` ([install.py#L255-L257](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/commands/install.py#L255-L257)). When a release's `Requires-Python` ruled out pipx's interpreter, pipx deleted the environment to rebuild it on another one. If that build failed, the user was left with an empty venv: no app, no injected packages, no `pipx_metadata.json`, and a message saying pipx had kept the venv. The next `pipx reinstall-all` then installed whatever project of that name the default index serves, without the original wheel, URL or `--index-url`. With this PR a failed rebuild puts the environment back. Fixes #2202.

title: 🔒 fix(interpreter): look up bare default python on PATH
bug_description:
When `PIPX_DEFAULT_PYTHON` held a command name or version such as `python3` or `3.15`, pipx first checked whether a file of that name existed in the current directory and, if so, used it as the default interpreter ([old lines](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/interpreter.py#L203-L210)). An executable `python3` left in the directory a user ran `pipx install` or `pipx run` from therefore ran as that user, and its path was saved as the environment's `source_interpreter`. After this PR a value without a path separator is looked up on `PATH` only. This addresses [draft advisory ANT-2026-6WOMZZ1B](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/security/advisories/GHSA-xhqr-j9g5-6pq4).

title: fix: load frontend plugin translations
bug_description:
## Problem

Strings coming from frontend plugins (e.g. modoboa-pro) were never translated:

- The host's vue3-gettext instance, shared with plugins through Module
  Federation, only contained the core catalog. Plugins compile their own
  `translations.json`, but nothing loaded it.
- Menu entries and statuses declared by plugins are translated by the API.
  At login, Django set a `django_language` cookie, and `LocaleMiddleware`
  gives it priority over the `Accept-Language` header the frontend sends with

  module that holds the plugin's compiled catalog (e.g. `"./translations"`).
  The serializer now passes it through to the frontend.

  the host ca

title: 🐛 fix(runpip): skip values of abbreviated options
bug_description: After a successful `pipx runpip ENV install ...`, pipx re-reads the arguments to find the main package's new source, and [skips the value of an option only when the option's name is an exact entry of its table](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/commands/run_pip.py#L133-L138). pip also accepts abbreviated long options, so `pipx runpip corp-tool install --only-bin corp-tool ./corp_tool-1.1-py3-none-any.whl` installs the wheel while pipx records the bare name `corp-tool` as the source. The next `pipx upgrade`, `upgrade-all` or `reinstall` then installs `corp-tool` from the configured index instead of the user's wheel, without any message. An abbreviated `--editable`, such as `--edit PATH`, was read the same way and recorded the project as a plain, non-editable spec. With this PR the abbreviated option's value is skipped like the full spelling's, the wheel path is recorded, and an abbreviated `--editable` records an editable install. Fixes

title: 🔒 fix(manifest): keep recorded args on sync
bug_description:
When a tool's environment already existed, `pipx manifest sync` reinstalled it with empty installer and venv arguments ([`manifest.py#L70-L85`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/commands/manifest.py#L70-L85)) and ignored the ones recorded in its `pipx_metadata.json`. If the tool had been installed with `--index-url PRIVATE`, the sync resolved its name on the installer's default index, PyPI unless configured otherwise. Anyone holding that name there got their release installed behind the tool's command, and the sync still exited 0. The empty arguments were then written back as the new record, so every later `pipx upgrade` and `pipx reinstall` used the default index too. With this PR, sync replays the recorded `pip_args` and `venv_args` of an existing environment, the same way `pipx reinstall` does. This addresses [draft advisory ANT-2026-Y8DNWZ8Q](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/security/advisories/GHSA-475f-3983-rp27).

After this PR, `pipx manifest lock` refuses the manifest before it runs nab or touches any file when a lock resolves outside the manifest directory. Fixes #2201.

title: 🔒 fix(run): start -c launchers with python -P
bug_description: `pipx run` started a script fetched from a URL or read from a named pipe as `python -c CONTENT` ([old lines](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/commands/run.py#L232-L241)), and the launcher for a `[pipx.run]` entry point, or for any console script run with `--python-args`, as `python -c CODE` ([old lines](https://github.com/pypa/pipx/blob/1d7102faf7f28c7bc46f4ffda56c015d186117dd/src/pipx/venv.py#L759-L765)). title: 🐛 fix(api): raise when a media dir is a file
bug_description:
With `ensure_exists`, a media directory the user configured through an `XDG_*_DIR` variable or `user-dirs.dirs` could point at a regular file, and platformdirs returned the file's path. `_optionally_create_media_directory` suppressed every `FileExistsError` so that dangling links to unmounted storage keep working (#561), and that also hid file collisions.

It now re-raises `FileExistsError` unless the path is a symlink whose target is missing. A regular file or a symlink to one raises; dangling links and symlink loops are returned unchanged, and symlinks to directories never raise. This covers the XDG variables, `user-dirs.dirs` and the module-level media functions such as `user_documents_path`.

`compute_checksum()` built its SHA-256 input by pasting the 16 hashed fields together with nothing between them, so two records that differed only in where a field boundary fell produced the same digest, and a row rewritten across a boundary still passed `verify_checksum()` and `verify_chain()`. `used_entities` had the same hole once joined: `["a,b"]` and `["a", "b"]` collided.

This replaces that encoding with one where a boundary cannot move, and records the encoding version on each row so a store written before the change keeps verifying instead of reporting a broken chain on upgrade.

```
title: fix(uwsgi): disable `sys.monitoring` if fork hooks are not run
bug_description:
## Description

This fixes a crash happening under uWSGI when the startup line doesn't use either `--lazy-apps`, `--py-call-uwsgi-fork-hooks` or `--py-call-osafterfork`. When that happens, the post-fork hooks aren't called post-fork, such that CPython's thread-related state isn't reset. Turning on a `sys.monitoring` event (e.g. `set_events` or `restart_events`) makes Python walk every thread state's frame chain, which can crash when a thread actually doesn't exist anymore. 

The proposed "fix" for this failure mode is to disable `sys.monitoring`-based features of the profiler altogether when post-fork hooks aren't run (which is detected through a new `forked_without_fork_hooks` function which inspects `uwsgi.opt`).

It's likely every feature of `ddtrace` that relies on `sys.monitoring` is exposed to the same kind of failure, so we should audit them.

title: fix(argo-workflows): run argo-server with TLS so SSO keeps deep links
bug_description:
## Problem

After "Login via single sign-on", Argo Workflows drops the user on the base href / last-used namespace instead of the page they originally requested (e.g. a deep link to `/workflows/<namespace>`).

## Root cause

argo-server decides whether to honour the post-login redirect by comparing it with a prefix built from its own `--secure` flag only (`server/auth/sso/sso.go`, `HandleCallback`: prefix = `http(s)://<host><base-href>`). The chart ran argo-server with `--secure=false`, so the prefix is `http://...`, while every browser URL is `https://...` (TLS terminated at the ALB or at the CDN in front of it). The requested redirect therefore never matches the prefix, is discarded, and the user lands on the default page.

## Change

- `templates/install.yaml`: `--secure=false` -> `--secure=true` (argo-server serves a self-signed, in-memory certificate); readiness probe `scheme: HTTP` -> `HTTPS`. Inline comment explains why TLS is enabled even though it is also terminated upstream.
```

title: fix(adapters): resolve an adapter for SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models (#715)
bug_description:
Closes #715 · Part of dogfood epic #701 (found in the Polar spike, #703)

## Problem

The plain-SQLAlchemy adapter was registered on `DeclarativeMeta`, a **metaclass**, while `AdapterRegistry.find_adapter_for_model` walks the model's **MRO**. A metaclass never appears in a class's MRO, so:

- SQLAlchemy 2.0 `DeclarativeBase` / `DeclarativeBaseNoMeta` / `MappedAsDataclass` models → `AdapterNotFoundError`
- legacy `declarative_base()` models → also `AdapterNotFoundError` (their MRO contains the generated `Base`, not `DeclarativeMeta`)

The existing `SQLAlchemyAdapter` tests use SQLModel models, which is why this went unnoticed.

## Change

- `adapters/__init__.py`: also register `SQLAlchemyAdapter` for `DeclarativeBase` and `DeclarativeBaseNoMeta`.
- `adapters/registry.py`: after the model's MRO, fall back to the metaclass's MRO (covers legacy `declarative_base()`). The class MRO is checked first, so SQLModel models (whose metaclass subclasses `DeclarativeMeta`) keep `SQLModelAdapter`.

title: [CUDA] Use redux.sync for eligible full-warp reductions
bug_description:
## Problem

Ordinary cross-thread reductions such as `T.reduce_max` still use a shuffle tree even when a full warp can use `redux.sync`. On main `837486a`, four independent 32-lane FP32 max reductions compiled for `sm_103a` with CUDA 13.1 produce 20 shuffle instructions and no redux. - Reuse `warp_reduce` from scalar and batched `AllReduce` stages whenever the group is a warp-aligned, unit-stride full warp. title: Implementing the shot-noise term for the momentum power spectrum
bug_description:
Implementing the shot-noise term for the Gaussian covariance matrix of the momentum auto-power spectrum. The random file will need an extra column called "VAR_U" that corresponds to the modelled variance of the velocity field at position x. We can model the uncertainty in the velocity measurement as \beta * H_0*D_c, where \beta is the relative uncertainty in peculiar velocity measurements (~20% for Tully-Fisher and the Fundamental Plane, ~5% for Type Ia supernovae). The variance should be the uncertainty plus the nonlinear velocity dispersion (usually set to 300 km/s). The main changes are:

1. As shown in equation 2.6, there is no \alpha in the shot-noise expression for the momentum power spectrum. The code is set up to set alpha = 0 when calculating the momentum power spectrum. 
2. An additional "velocity" boolean parameter, which is set to true when we are calculating the velocity power spectrum. 
3. The extra variance term is multiplied onto the grid before applying the FFT algorit

```
title: Keep secrets out of database error text
bug_description:
SQLAlchemy writes a failed statement's bound values into the text of its error, and no engine hid them, so every log line that formats a database error carried what the statement bound. The session check binds the visitor's session token. When its connection dies mid-query, the sign-in check logs the outage at ERROR, and that line held the token. Agent logins had the same problem in another form. `CREATE ROLE` takes no parameters, so the password was part of the SQL text, which a failed creation repeats in the web log and Postgres repeats in its own.

The engines now set `hide_parameters`, so neither errors nor the echo log show bound values, and agent logins are created with the password's SCRAM verifier computed in the web, which logs the container in but cannot be turned back into the password.

title: Write a job's cost as it runs
bug_description:
A run wrote its cost record once, at the very end. When the web stopped a container on a cancel, a restart or a timeout, Python ran as PID 1 without a SIGTERM handler, so docker killed it after ten seconds and the record was never written, and the worker's cleanup force-removed the container as well. Cancelled and timed-out jobs therefore had no cost at all, and a failed write at the end was only a warning.

A run now writes one record per iteration and one for the report, each holding the tokens spent since the last saved record. A failed write carries its tokens into the next record, and a last write that fails logs every count. The container turns SIGTERM into a cancel, cleanup gives it ten seconds before removing it, and a cancelled omp turn counts the messages it had already finished. The billing table shows each record's iteration.
```

title: Retry or raise database errors on job-state paths
bug_description:
Job-state code turned database errors into ordinary answers. A failed read looked like a missing job, a failed write looked like a refused transition, and a failed list looked like no jobs. A short outage could therefore fail a healthy job, keep a finished one `running` and holding its slot for up to four hours, answer 404 for a job that exists, skip startup recovery, or leave a queued job waiting on an idle server.

Connection errors are now told apart from other database errors, and only they are retried. Agent containers wait up to 30 seconds for the database on every connect and on status reads and writes, then fail, and the job's error carries the container's reason. The web's request paths fail at once, and the API answers 503. Its background work, meaning the worker's final write, startup recovery and the queue pick, keeps retrying until the database is back.

Stacked on #342.

title: Guard job status writes by their prior status
bug_description:
Every job status write was unconditional, so the web and the agent container overwrote each other. A cancelled queued job was relaunched by its worker, a cancel could drop a live thread from the slot count, a queued job could be picked twice, and the container's final status could replace a cancel or a timeout. Building a JobManager, as the CLI and the dev reload do, cancelled every running job of the live web.

Each write now names the statuses it may leave and applies only from those, and the writer acts on a refusal: a worker does not launch, a container stops. Restart recovery runs only at web startup. It cancels jobs whose container was lost and starts the queued and pending ones instead of cancelling them. A job waiting for feedback can now be cancelled, and queued jobs start oldest first.

The transition table behind these rules is in the cleanup plan, one row per event against every status.

title: AC-528: feat(shared): opt-in preview tokens so confirm=true cannot skip the preview
bug_description:
## Summary

In `confirm` mode the preview is advisory. The tool branches on `if not confirm` and nothing records that a preview happened, so a client can send `confirm=true` on its first call and never see one. SECURITY.md ("Preview-Before-Confirm") says so. This PR adds an opt-in mode that closes the gap and changes nothing when it's off.

- **`UNIFI_REQUIRE_PREVIEW_TOKEN=true`** (or `UNIFI_<NETWORK|PROTECT|ACCESS>_REQUIRE_PREVIEW_TOKEN`, which wins) makes every successful preview response carry a `preview_token` and `preview_token_expires_in`. title: Fix printing of floating-point constants whose exponent ends in zero
bug_description:
`ConstantPrinter.print_constant()` formats a float with `f"{x:#.9g}"`. The `#` flag keeps the decimal point and the trailing zeros. Then `.rstrip("0")` removes these zeros.

In scientific notation, the string ends with the exponent. Thus `.rstrip("0")` also removes zeros from the exponent:

| Constant | Printed | Read back as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1e-10` | `1.00000000e-1` | `0.1` |
| `7.5e-10` | `7.50000000e-1` | `0.75` |
| `1e10` | `1.00000000e+1` | `10.0` |

All code generators and the ODE-toolbox interface print constants with `ConstantPrinter`. #1296 added the `.rstrip("0")` call, and #1400 moved it into `ConstantPrinter`. NESTML 8.3.0 and 9.0.0 include it.

### Does this occur in normal use?

Yes, for some values. A constant is affected when it prints in scientific notation and its exponent ends in zero. Scientific notation is used for absolute values below 1e-4, and for 1e9 and above. Examples are `1e-10`, `2.5e-10`, `1e10` and `1e-20`. The value can also come from a unit conv

## Description
<!-- What issue or task does this change relate to? -->

Processors are meant to refuse dropout when the model is sharded across GPUs. Ranks in a model group share a random seed, so dropout on sharded data draws correlated masks instead of independent ones. That check never ran. It lived in `BaseProcessor.forward`, and every processor we implement overrides `forward` without calling it. Mappers never had the check at all, though the transformer mappers take `dropout_p`.

Every processor's `forward`, and the `forward` of the four intermediate mapper bases (graph transformer, GNN, point-wise, transformer), now starts with `refuse_dropout_when_sharded(self, model_comm_group)`. Every concrete mapper reaches one of those directly or through `super().forward`. It raises `ValueError` when the module is training, the model is sharded, and anything in it drops: a dropout layer or a `dropout_p` (attention) above zero. title: [Ascend] Preserve buffer view layouts and pointer units
bug_description:
Buffers created with `T.view` or `T.reshape` can share storage while requiring different layouts. Resolving layouts through the shared data variable can select the wrong Cube mapping or DMA address, and stale allocation geometry can lose version offsets or misinterpret typed pointer offsets.

### Summary
Fix an issue where large agent responses get truncated by context management before being returned to the caller.

### The Problem
When the agent generates a valid but lengthy response, context management compresses it into a short preview for history. The app then pulls the final result from this pruned history, receiving an incomplete answer and often triggering unnecessary retry loops or degraded returns.

## Overview

The Elastic EP Scaling test (distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling) failed with AITER on. The cause is:
1. AITER requires a torch.distributed-registered group, but Elastic EP is using stateless group, which is not torch.distributed registered at all, so we need to skip AITER AR and choose next available AR;
2. During scale-up, existing workers call _release_cuda_graphs() and then re-capture into the same global graph pool. Some memory in that pool was still allocated, because FlyDSL didn't release them correctly. Graph replay never re-enters Python, so a kernel last launched during capture holds those tensors inside the graph pool indefinitely. The pool had no graphs left but still had live blocks, so PyTorch rejected capturing into it again. Now I explicitly call _switch_to_fresh_graph_pool() to switch to a new graph pool to avoid this.

## Claims

These 2 bugs are fixed. This test case works as expected no matter AITER is on or off.

## Summary

Native search, file preview, or attachment loading can open the Harness UI metadata database in the same process as SQLite. Closing these ordinary file handles can release SQLite's locks, allowing another connection to remove still-live WAL/SHM files. ## Description

`HeadroomClient` ignored `HeadroomConfig.store_url`. The constructor copied `config.store_url` into `self._store_url`, but then opened storage with its own `store_url` argument:

title: Fix: preserve direction and input identity in memoized evaluations

`MemoizeOperator` currently treats a cached forward `(x, Ax)` pair as an adjoint result, returning `x` for `A.H @ (A @ x)`. title: fix(transforms): stop an embedded markdown table from dropping the rest of a tool result
bug_description:
## Description

A tool result that contains a markdown table is rewritten as JSON of the table's rows. Everything else in the result is dropped without a marker: headings, prose, and the output of other commands in the same Bash call. A later line with pipes is parsed as a row too.

Root cause: `_try_detect_markdown_table` claims the whole payload as `TABULAR` (0.95) as soon as a header and separator pair appears anywhere in its first 50 lines. The tabular compressor then parses it with `parse_markdown_table`, which keeps only lines containing `|`. Its savings check compares the JSON against the full original text, so dropping the prose counts as compression. Markdown tables are not detected by the Rust side, which only returns `Tabular` for git status. On the native backend, plain text falls back to this same Python detector, and `parse_tabular` re-runs it. So this function decides the route on both backends.

The fix treats content as a markdown table only when it is one: the header

## Summary

`_module_members` built its import-subtraction set by walking `tree.body` only, so an import nested in top-level control flow never entered it and survived Jedi's module-scope `get_names` as a member. `outline` and `inspect.edge_counts.members` over-counted in lockstep — every module importing `JediAnalyzer` under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` listed it as a child.

Two findings widened the fix beyond the issue as filed:

- The leak is **not TYPE_CHECKING-specific** — a `try`/`except ImportError` shim leaks identically, as does any conditional guard.

So both edges now share one walk, `_iter_module_scope_imports`: `members` **subtracts** what it yields, `imports` **emits** it — they cannot drift apart again. The rule is **binding scope, not nesting**: descend

title: fix(openclaw/release): ship responsive npm integrations
bug_description:
## Description

Fixes #977 and #2353.

The v0.35.0 release built all three JavaScript packages successfully, but npm rejected every publish with ENEEDAUTH. Because each publish step used continue-on-error, the publish-npm job still concluded success. npm therefore remains on headroom-ai 0.22.4 and headroom-openclaw 0.1.0, while headroom-opencode is absent.

The checked-in OpenClaw source had already corrected the old strict-schema mismatch and added a circuit breaker, but its assemble hook still called compression for every tiny conversation and allowed a 30-second default wait. This PR completes both the runtime correction and the delivery path instead of merely exposing one failure.

## Changes

### OpenClaw runtime

- Skip proxy compression below an 800-character context floor (roughly 200 tokens), avoiding synchronous HTTP work on short conversations that cannot produce meaningful savings.
- Measure actual content, including tool-call arguments, so a single large tool result remain

title: Fix static `tsave` inside stochastic solvers
bug_description:
> [!NOTE]
> This description and the implementation in 85e16e43 were written by Claude (AI), at the request of @gautierronan.

The fixed step SSE/SME methods (`EulerJump`, `EulerMaruyama`, `Rouchon1`) required a static `tsave`, converted to a tuple, because the number of steps per save interval set the length of a `lax.scan`. As a result, these solvers:

- could not be called inside `jax.jit`, even with a constant `tsave` (`ConcretizationTypeError`),
- recompiled for every new `tsave`,
- required a linearly spaced `tsave`.

This PR makes `tsave` (and `dt`) regular traced arrays in `dq.jssesolve()`, `dq.dssesolve()`, `dq.jsmesolve()`, `dq.dsmesolve()` and the `JumpMonteCarlo`/`DiffusiveMonteCarlo` methods of `dq.mesolve()`.

## Implementation
